actions.summary: Strengthen later-quarter non-authority language in the main planner prompt.

details.needle: "- the displayed Q2 through Q20 row values are intentionally blank; do not infer hidden defaults from them\n",
details.snippet: "- every Q2 through Q20 cell must be actively chosen from business reality and the hard cash law rather than reconstructed from placeholder history\n",

actions.summary: Remove raw fixed-facts model views from the AI-facing planning-mode payload.
Widen capex / schedule deployment behavior in the first failing window.

details.needle: "In particular, do not leave Capital Expenditures, Principal Repayments, debt movement rows, or Net Additions as tiny or repeated placeholder-like ranges if the cash posture requires real deployment.\n",
details.snippet: "When the first failing quarter shows cash still above band, widen the relevant schedule-style deployment rows materially in that quarter and the immediately following window rather than making only cosmetic increases.\n",

actions.summary: Relax later-quarter cash posture where the business cannot credibly absorb the surplus.

details.needle: "If the business is likely to generate more cash than it can credibly redeploy in a given horizon, relax the cash path instead of forcing an unrealistically low balance.\n",
details.snippet: "If a quarter would only be feasible with implausibly small retained cash or implausibly large deployment, widen that quarter and the next few quarters rather than forcing the planner into infeasible bands.\n",
details.recommendation: Relax the later-quarter cash path or add materially wider deployment capacity where the first failing quarter breaks. Strengthen capital-allocation rows in the first failing window rather than relying on small schedule ranges. actions.summary: Strengthen non-cash planning pressure against an overpowered operating engine.

details.needle: "- if the cash law requires meaningful deployment or absorption, you are expected to move discretionary non-cash rows materially after Q1 when that is what a believable business would do\n",
details.snippet: "- if the operating engine still generates excess cash after that, you must also moderate the operating rows realistically rather than assuming deployment rows alone can absorb everything\n",
